messages:
maria: quick sync 1: thinking about a simpler ownership-first model for service keys. proposal: every API/service key has an explicit owner claim (team_id + human_owner). primary goals: easier audits, scoped revokes, and clearer billing attribution. question: how do we handle cross-team service-to-service calls without giving universal privileges?

 tj: +1. owner claim makes audits trivial. for cross-team calls we should use an exchange service that mints short-lived, audience-restricted tokens. avoid expanding long-lived keys.

 alex: agree on exchange. perf will be the main concern. naive per-request exchange is too expensive. propose gateway-level caching of exchanged tokens with conservative TTL and revocation hooks.

 maria: two-mode flow sketch:
 1) intra-team calls: direct use of owner-scoped key (no exchange).
 2) cross-team calls: caller uses its long-lived key to request an ephemeral audience-bound token from auth-broker, then call downstream with ephemeral.

 tj: auth-broker API sketch (starting point):
 POST /v1/exchange 
 body: {"from_key_id":"...","audience":"svc-b","intent":"read:catalog"} 
 response: {"token":"...","exp":<unix>}
 broker validation: verify from_key active, check policy (is from_key allowed to request audience svc-b for the requested intent), ledger the request for audit.

 jamal: product + UX ask: need a centralized key inventory UI showing key_id, owner (team + person), linked services, last rotated, creation source (manual/saas/onboarding), active exchanges count. also a support API for key lookups.

 alex: caching details: gateway caches {from_key_id,audience,intent} -> ephemeral token for min(exp, cache_ttl). on broker-side revocation or key rotation, broker publishes a revocation event on a pubsub topic; gateways subscribed will drop matching cache entries.

 maria: sample ephemeral JWT claim set we'd expect (informal):
 ```
{
  "iss":"auth-broker.redwood",
  "sub":"svc-a.team-x",
  "aud":"svc-b.team-y",
  "owner":"team-x",
  "intent":"read:catalog",
  "iat":1700000000,
  "exp":1700000300
}
```

 tj: policy model: two orthogonal checks: 1) key-level policy (does key X have permission to request audience Y/intents?), 2) org-level policy (is team X allowed to act on behalf of team X across org boundaries?). Admin role can bypass but is logged/flagged.

 jamal: customer config: support both explicit cross-team grants (team Y explicitly allows team X to call) and an audit-logged request flow where ops can retro-approve. some enterprise customers will want pre-approved allowlists.

 alex: batch-exchange for fanout jobs: broker issues a batch token listing multiple audiences and allowed intents. token contains a signed list and short TTL (e.g., 20 minutes). broker still validates and records each audience in ledger to keep audit fidelity.

 maria: security tradeoffs: batch tokens increase blast radius if leaked but reduce broker load. mitigate with very short TTL, audience restriction, and mandatory per-audience consent in policy for high-sensitivity services.

 tj: RBAC surface: map roles -> audience scopes + max_ttl. example table: [ ["service-basic": audiences within same project, ttl 5m], ["cross-caller": explicit grant required, ttl 5m], ["ops-admin": wildcard audience, ttl 1m but flagged in audit] ]. store mappings in policy DB accessible to broker.

 jamal: telemetry: emit metrics per owner_key: exchange_requests, exchange_rejects, active_ephemerals, cache_hits, revocations. UI dashboard to detect unusual spikes (possible abuse).

 alex: rollout plan: 1) opt-in owner claim on new keys + UI inventory, 2) run broker in permissive mode (issue tokens but mark calls), 3) enable gateway caching + revocation listener, 4) flip enforcement for a small service subset, 5) expand org-wide.

 maria: operational notes: long-lived keys should only be minting primitives; hide them behind vaults and restrict distribution. require rotation policy and enforce creation reasons.

 tj: edge-case: cron/background workers that make many downstream calls. for these, prefer a signed batch token or pre-warmed ephemeral pool with strict TTLs and limited audience set. include a "purpose" claim to link to job run id for traceability.

 jamal: support implications: need APIs for listing active ephemerals for a key (for debugging), a revoke endpoint (revoke key or revoke individual ephemeral by jti), and webhook for key lifecycle events to inform downstream deploys.

 alex: compatibility/backwards-compat: allow current long-lived keys to keep working while we add owner property. broker can accept legacy keys by inferring owner from attached metadata until teams migrate.

 maria: agreed action items: I'll draft a short RFC doc with diagrams and example claims. @tj please draft broker API endpoints, policy data model, and audit ledger format. @alex please prototype gateway cache + revocation handler and the batch token format. @jamal please design key inventory UI and telemetry dashboard fields.

 tj: will produce API & policy draft by EOW.

 alex: will spike on cache invalidation this week.

 jamal: will sketch UI mockups and telemetry panels.

 deploy-bot: deploy notice: auth-broker/v2 scheduled canary -> 2025-02-20T06:00Z :rocket:

 maria: great sync. i'll tag the RFC PR when it's ready and link mocks. thanks all :thumbsup:
